title: Salut !
subtitle: Hello, how are you, goodbye
review: Written by Claude. Check the French, the English lines, the notes and the questions.
intro: A greeting meant for the cat, a car that no longer runs, a man who leaves for work three times and an urgent appointment in the bedroom: four short scenes between Emma and Lucas. Listen for how they say hello, ask how things are, and say goodbye.

lines.note: Coucou is affectionate: for family, friends and children.
Bonsoir replaces bonjour from late afternoon.

tr.en: Good evening, my princess! How are you?

lines.note: Comment allez-vous ? uses vous: the formal question. Here it is a joke.

lines.text: Oh ! Très bien, merci. Et vous ?

tr.en: Oh! Very well, thank you. And you?
I was talking to the cat.

lines.note: Salut is casual, and toi replaces vous: the cat got the formal greeting.

lines.text: Salut. Ta princesse a mangé ton dîner.

tr.en: Hi. Your princess has eaten your dinner.

lines.note: Ça va is both the question and the answer.
Tranquille: everything is calm, nothing to report.

tr.en: And the car? Running all right?

lines.note: Ça roule ? means 'all good?'. Rouler also means to run, of a car: that is the joke.
Bof is a shrug in one word: not great.
Spoken French drops ne: elle ne roule plus.
J'y vais: I'm going. Bon announces it.
À + a time: see you then. À ce soir, à demain, à lundi.

lines.text: C'est encore moi. Mes clés. À plus !

tr.en: Me again. My keys. See you later!

lines.note: À plus is short for à plus tard. Casual.

lines.text: Mon téléphone. À tout à l'heure !

tr.en: My phone. See you in a bit!

lines.note: À tout à l'heure: later the same day.

lines.text: Cette fois, c'est la bonne. Au revoir !

tr.en: This time I mean it. Goodbye!

lines.note: C'est la bonne: this is the right one, the time it works.
À bientôt: soon, with no fixed time.

lines.text: Oh, déjà cette heure-là ! Bon, je vais y aller.

tr.en: Oh, is that the time! Right, I'm going to head off.

lines.note: Bon, je vais y aller: the polite way to start leaving.

lines.text: Faut que j'y aille, c'est tout. Je te laisse !

tr.en: I've got to go, that's all. I'll leave you to it!

lines.note: Faut que j'y aille = il faut que j'y aille. Je te laisse ends a chat or a call.

lines.text: Pas le temps. Je file ! On s'appelle !

tr.en: No time. Must dash! Let's talk soon!

lines.note: Je file: I'm rushing off. On s'appelle: we'll phone each other.

lines.text: Alors prends la poubelle en passant. Et tiens-moi au courant.

tr.en: Then take the bin on your way. And keep me posted.

lines.note: Tiens-moi au courant: tell me what happens.

notes: Bonjour by day, bonsoir from late afternoon. Salut and coucou are for people you say tu to.
Comment allez-vous ? is formal (vous). With friends: ça va ?, ça roule ?, quoi de neuf ?
Ça va is the question and the answer. Bof, ça va means 'not great'. Tranquille means 'all quiet'.
À + a time says when you will meet again: à tout à l'heure (later today), à ce soir, à demain, à bientôt (soon, no date). À plus is casual.
To leave, announce it first: bon, je vais y aller; faut que j'y aille; je file.
Spoken French drops ne and il: elle roule plus, faut que j'y aille.

questions.q: It is 8 p.m. and you walk into a shop. What do you say?
questions.why: Bonsoir from late afternoon. Coucou is only for people you know well.

questions.q: Lucas says « Comment allez-vous ? » to the cat and « Salut » to Emma. Why is that funny?
options: The cat gets the formal greeting.
questions.why: Comment allez-vous ? uses vous, the polite form. Salut is the casual one.

questions.q: « Ça roule ? » « Bof, ça va. » How is Lucas?
questions.why: Bof is a shrug: so-so, not great.

questions.q: You will see your friend again in two hours. What do you say?
questions.why: À tout à l'heure: later the same day.

questions.q: You want to end a phone call politely. What do you say?
questions.why: Je te laisse: 'I'll let you go'.
